Definition: from G4253 and a derivative of G4969; previously (recently) slain (fresh), i.e. (figuratively) lately made:--new.
BiblicalUsage: Prosphatos, as an adjective, means newly made, fresh, lately slain. It appears once, of the way Christ opened: by a new and living way, which He hath consecrated for us, through the veil, that is to say, His flesh.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the way is new because it was never open before, and living because the One who opened it lives forever.
